name: object-type-scoped-target-collision
description: Two rules from different object types share an op_type, field, and target — the same shape spec.FieldRules() produces today for the 'labels' target (document's string label vs review/issue's object-ref label), collapsed here onto a single op_type 'tag' so a normalizing and a non-normalizing value_type visibly disagree. object_type 'beta' declares 'add' as a person-ref (normalizing) OR-set; unrelated object_type 'alpha' declares the identical op_type/field/target as a plain string (non-normalizing) OR-set. The single op folded here is an 'alpha' object, so only the 'alpha' rule may govern it (spec/fold.md §5's object-type scoping) — the 'beta' rule must never match, however its target or op_type happen to line up. If object-type scoping is dropped from opMatchesRule, the 'beta' rule matches too: the engine's break-after-first-match dispatch normalizes the item and drops it into a single-item set with the wrong value, while the reference fold's un-broken per-op loop applies both rules and produces a two-item set — either way, a mismatch against expected_state.
